answers.Q3_business_goal: AI agents increasingly need to call third-party services but today's patterns leave the live credential in the agent's process memory, provide no per-request audit, and make rotation a code change. Mintkey solves this by brokering access: agents discover services via MCP, receive a scoped short-lived JWT, and call backends through an egress proxy that injects the real credential — which the agent never sees.

Q25_risks.title: Egress Proxy compromise exposes plaintext credentials
Q25_risks.what_breaks: Attacker with code execution in the proxy plugin reads plaintext credentials from process memory during request mutation

Q25_risks.title: JWT signing key compromise enables arbitrary token minting
Q25_risks.what_breaks: Attacker with the Ed25519 private key can mint valid JWTs for any agent, service, and tenant — bypassing all permission checks

Q25_risks.title: Audit coverage gap allows undetected state mutation
Q25_risks.what_breaks: A code path that mutates state without calling audit.emit() creates a silent gap; forensic investigation misses the event; compliance audit fails
